rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 - two-season greenhouse experiment (2024) on red clay soil in Changsha with cucumbers under subsurface drip irrigation, three DO levels of micro-nano bubble water x three biochar rates plus CK, randomized block design with three replicates. Q2: Section 3.6 / Fig. 9 - DO concentration in MNBW had a highly significant effect on cucumber yield (P<0.01); yield rose significantly as DO rose; VC, organic acid and sugar-acid ratio were significantly affected by DO; average yield up 1.72-44.23% versus CK. Q4: Sections 3.1, 3.4, 3.7 / Figs. 3, 7, 10 - soil oxygen and redox potential rose significantly with DO; net photosynthetic rate rose; Pearson analysis shows SO, SAP, Pn and dry weight positively correlated with yield (P<0.05).
rows.notes: Aerated (MNBW) subsurface drip vs non-aerated: the factorial ANOVA isolates the DO main effect on yield and quality, though the CK comparison is confounded with biochar (CK has no biochar). Single site, single soil, single crop, plot scale; only letter groupings and p-values reported, no SD/CI; no explicit limitations beyond 'more research'. Soluble sugars and soluble solids were not significantly affected, so quality improvement is partial (VC, SAR).

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 - own two-season greenhouse field experiment with cucumbers under micro-nano aerated subsurface drip irrigation and biochar.
rows.notes: The study does not measure pesticide use, pests or diseases at all; it reports soil aeration, photosynthesis, dry matter, yield, quality and water use efficiency. No evidence on reduced pesticide applications.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 - own two-season greenhouse experiment, cucumbers, red clay soil, subsurface drip with three DO levels of MNBW and three biochar rates plus CK. Q2: Sections 3.3-3.6 / Figs. 6-9 - DO in MNBW significantly increased plant height, stem diameter, net photosynthetic rate, total dry weight, yield, IWUE and WUE (P<0.05 to P<0.01); yield up 1.72-44.23%, dry matter up 10.53-69.19% versus CK. Q4: Sections 3.1, 3.4, 3.7 / Figs. 3, 7, 10 - soil oxygen and redox potential measured and rose with DO; Pn measured; correlation analysis links SO, SAP, Pn and dry weight to yield (P<0.05).
rows.notes: Crop performance claim is supported by the DO main effect in the factorial design. One site, one soil, one crop, two consecutive seasons; plot scale in a greenhouse; results given as percent ranges and letter groupings only, no dispersion measures; no explicit limitations stated; conditions (e.g. biochar type, climate) mentioned only as possible reasons for discrepancies with other studies, not as requirements.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.4 - own two-season greenhouse experiment with soil sensors (TEROS12, FireSting-O2, ORP meter, ring-knife bulk density). Q2: Section 3.1 / Fig. 3 - DO concentration in MNBW significantly raised soil oxygen content and soil redox potential (P<0.01) with significant DO x biochar interaction; average SO up 0.47-31.80% and SRP up 0.54-34.74% versus CK; Section 4.1 attributes SO/SORP gains to oxygen-rich MNBW.
rows.notes: Aerated water improved soil oxygen and redox potential, but had no significant effect on bulk density, porosity, aeration porosity or soil water content; those improvements came from biochar. 'Soil condition' is thus only partly supported for the aeration component. Soil oxygen and redox potential are different indicators measured by different meters rather than two methods confirming one result, so Q3 is 'no'. No SD/CI reported in text, single site and soil, plot scale, no stated limitations.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a two-factor (DO in micro-nano bubble water x biochar) greenhouse experiment; CK lacks biochar, so comparisons to CK confound aeration and biochar, but ANOVA main effects for DO are reported separately. Figures could not be inspected for error bars; text reports only letter groupings, p-values and percent ranges across treatments.
